Raoul Kanme Scores Seven-Figure Win In Triton ONE North Cyprus Main Event

Dutch Player Bests 1,006 Entries In $8,000 Buy-In To Earn $1,320,000

by Erik Fast | Published: Nov 15, 2026 | E-mail Author

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:27
Instaread

The 2026 Triton ONE North Cyprus $8,000 no-limit hold’em main event drew a massive field of 1,006 entries to create a $7,316,638 prize pool. As a result, the first-place prize swelled to $1,320,000. That sizable sum was ultimately seized by Raoul Kanme, who emerged victorious from the sizable turnout at Merit Royal Hotel with his first Triton ONE title and the second seven-figure score of his career.

“Throughout three or four days I was playing my game, not too crazy, waiting for my spots,” Kanme told Triton staff after closing out the triumph. “And the final table today I started in fifth place, I just waited for my hands, got lucky one time with A-5 against pocket tens, but it happens. That’s poker, you know, and I think the rest of my game was pretty good. The heads-up might have been messy, but I won anyway, so who cares.”

The 36-year-old Dutch player now has more than $3.7 million in lifetime earnings, after winning a $25,000 buy-in at the Onyx Super High Roller Series at this same venue back in August for $1,250,000.

Kanme is now ranked 64th in the 2026 Card Player Player of the Year standings, thanks in large part to his two momentous wins in North Cyprus. The latest windfall of 1,920 points brought his total to 3,508 in the yearlong race, which is presented by CoinPoker.

This event ran from Nov. 10-15, with three starting flights ahead of a trio of combined-field sessions. The top 159 finishers made the money, with big names like Leon Sturm (40th), Terrance Reid (38th), Ren Lin (30th), Ding Biao (16th), and Danilo Velasevic (14th) among those to run deep.

Big Names Fall Early At The Final Table

The final day began with three Triton Super High Roller champions still in contention: chip leader Alex Anton, Paulius Vaitiekunas, and five-time trident trophy winner Mikita Badziakouski.

Aleksei Istomin (9th – $98,000) was the first to fall, with a brutal runout for his A♥Q♣ against the A♠Q♥ of Thore Boedefeld. The board brought four spades to give Boedefeld a winning flush.

Vaitiekunas then lost a preflop flip with A♣K♥ against the pocket tens of Mohamed El Wely to hit the rail in eighth place ($127,038). 

Anton fell out of the lead during the early action. He had a chance to bounce back when he got all-in with pocket tens leading the A♠5♠ of Kanme. As he noted in his post-win quote, the runout went Kanme’s way: 5♣4♣2♣2♥3♣. Anton then lost a race with pocket nines against the A-Q of Zhuoqun Zhang to slide to the bottom of the leaderboard. He soon was all-in and at risk with A♠10♦ dominating the A♣8♥ of Boedefeld and the 10♥8♠ of Zhang. The board gave Zhang tens and eights to end Anton’s run in seventh place ($177,000).

That left Badziakouski as the lone trident trophy winner remaining. The Belarusian superstar ran 10♦9♦ into the K♠K♥ of Zhang, who flopped a set and turned a full house. Badziakouski had a single out with trip nines, but was unable to improve to quads on the end. He earned $235,000 for his sixth-place showing, increasing his career haul to nearly $73.3 million. As a result, he surpassed Adrian Mateos ($73.2 million) to move to fourth place on poker’s all-time money list.

Kanme Thrives Down The Stretch

Boedefeld’s final stand pitted K♥J♠ against the Q♥10♥ of Zhang. The short stack got all-in preflop with the better chance of winning, but a queen-high runout saw him eliminated in fifth place ($321,000).

Yiwen Yuan soon followed, with her J♠J♥ cracked with the A♠8♠ of El Wely, who flopped an ace and held from there. Yuan, who finished seventh in the ladies event earlier in the festival, earned a career-best $420,000 payday as the fourth-place finisher.

El Wely’s surge continued when his A♦K♥ held against the A♠J♦ of Zhang. The 5♠5♣3♦10♦5♦ runout kept El Wely ahead and ended Zhang’s tournament in third place ($561,000). This was a new personal best on the live circuit for the Chinese player.

Heads-up play began with El Wely holding roughly an 8:5 chip advantage over Kanme. Fairly early in the match, Kanme doubled with K-Q against pocket tens to overtake the lead.

El Wely’s stack continued to dwindle as play continued, but he was eventually able to mount a comeback. Kanme had just a handful of big blinds more than El Wely when the final hand of the tournament arrived. The chips got in with A♦Q♠ racing against 9♥9♣. The board of 10♠5♥3♣J♥Q♦ saw El Wely hold through the flop and turn, but Kanme spiked a pair of queens on the river to earn the pot and the title.

El Wely secured a career-best payday of $793,000 as the runner-up.
